case_relationship.rationale: This is an FAO market narrative about September 2026, not an observation from the Black Sea Grain Initiative's 2022-2023 corridor series.

publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

black_sea.summary: FAO stated that logistical disruptions in the Black Sea region reduced maize export availability and constrained sunflower-oil price declines despite expectations of ample supply.

alternative_origins.summary: FAO reported that Black Sea logistical constraints prompted importers to shift toward alternative origins.

simultaneous_factors_reported.summary: The same release also identified dry conditions in North America, lower-than-anticipated US yields, less export availability in Brazil, and uncertainty over Strait of Hormuz shipping with implications for fuel, fertilizer and freight costs.

interpretation_ceiling.allowed: Record values and explanations as a dated FAO-published observation, subject to exact source capture and revision review.
not_established: Independent confirmation of the FAO narrative or the relative contribution of each factor.
A quantified causal effect of conflict or shipping disruption on global prices.
A specific port closure, named supplier, shipment, inventory, destination shortage or real-time route state.
A current operational warning or forecast.
